title: The Evergreen Game
summary: The Evergreen Game is remembered for its sudden finish, in which Anderssen sacrifices his queen and a rook and ends with a bishop mate on e7. Black's queen raids on f5, h5 and f3 look greedy, and the engine shows how quickly the evaluation swings once White's pieces open lines against the king. Watch how the attack is built from loose pawns, open files and the bishop on d7.

moves.comment: 1.e4 takes the centre with the king's pawn and opens lines for the queen and bishop.
1...e5 mirrors the move and contests the centre directly.
2.Nf3 develops a knight and attacks the e5 pawn.
2...Nc6 defends e5 and develops another piece towards the centre.
3.Bc4 develops the bishop to an active diagonal aimed at f7. The engine slightly preferred 3.Bb5, so this is only a good move.
3...Bc5 mirrors White's bishop. The engine preferred 3...Nf6, so this is a good move rather than the best.
4.b4 offers a pawn to deflect the bishop. The engine preferred 4.c3, so this gambit is only a good try.
4...Bxb4 accepts the pawn and keeps the extra material.
5.c3 attacks the bishop on b4 and gains a tempo for White.
5...Ba5 keeps the bishop on the long diagonal and avoids being trapped.
6.d4 strikes at the centre and opens the position for White's pieces.
6...exd4 captures the pawn and opens the e-file. The engine preferred 6...d6, so this is only a good move.
7.O-O castles and brings the rook towards the centre. The engine preferred 7.Qb3 here, so this is a good move.
7...d3 pushes a passed pawn deep into White's camp. The engine preferred 7...Nge7, so this is a good move that gives White counterplay.
8.Qb3 attacks the advanced d3 pawn and the b5 and f7 squares.
8...Qf6 defends the d-pawn and the kingside while keeping the queen active.
9.e5 attacks the queen and gains space, forcing Black to move the queen again.
9...Qg6 keeps the queen safe and watches the kingside.
10.Re1 brings the rook to the open e-file. The engine preferred 10.Rd1, so this is a good move.
10...Nge7 develops the knight and guards the key squares around the king.
11.Ba3 develops the bishop to attack the d6 square. The engine preferred 11.Qd1, so this is a good move and the evaluation slips to -0.8.
11...b5 grabs space but loosens Black's queenside. The engine preferred 11...d5, and this is a mistake that hands White the initiative.

moment.title: Black loosens the queenside
moment.text: 11...b5 gives up the protection of the queenside pawns and the king's cover on that wing. The evaluation swings from -0.8 to +0.6, and the engine preferred 11...d5. Watch how the b-file opens for White's queen and rook.

moves.comment: 12.Qxb5 wins a pawn and places the queen on an active square. The engine preferred 12.Bxb5, so this is a good move.
12...Rb8 attacks the queen along the b-file and develops the rook.
13.Qa4 keeps the queen active and pins pressure on the black position.
13...Bb6 retreats the bishop to a safe square. The engine preferred 13...Bb7, so this is a good move.
14.Nbd2 develops the knight to support the attack. The engine preferred 14.Qd1, so this is a good move.
14...Bb7 places the bishop on a diagonal, but the evaluation jumps to +2.0. The engine preferred 14...O-O, so this is a mistake.
15.Ne4 centralises the knight and eyes the d6 and f6 squares.
15...Qf5 grabs material but allows a strong reply. The engine preferred 15...d2, and this blunder lets the evaluation rise to +6.2.

moment.title: The queen raid to f5
moment.text: 15...Qf5 looks like a free pawn grab, but it takes the queen away from the defence of the king. The evaluation jumps from +2.0 to +6.2, which is the largest swing in the game. Notice that the engine preferred 15...d2 instead.

moves.comment: 16.Bxd3 captures the d-pawn and adds to White's material lead.
16...Qh5 keeps the queen active. The engine preferred 16...Qe6, so this is a good move.
17.Nf6+ gives check with the knight, but the engine preferred 17.Ng3, and the evaluation drops from +6.7 to +0.7.

moment.title: The knight sacrifice on f6
moment.text: 17.Nf6+ gives up the knight, and the engine preferred 17.Ng3 which keeps the attack alive. After the recapture on f6 the evaluation falls to +0.7, so the sacrifice did not win by force. Watch how the position still carries White's pressure.

moves.comment: 17...gxf6 captures the knight, which is the natural and best reply.
18.exf6 recaptures and opens the e-file for the rook.
18...Rg8 contests the open g-file with the rook.
19.Rad1 places a rook on the open d-file. The engine preferred 19.Be4, so this is a good move.
19...Qxf3 takes a knight but the evaluation jumps to +5.0. The engine preferred 19...Qh3, so this is a blunder that lets White's attack take over.

moment.title: Black takes the f3 knight
moment.text: 19...Qxf3 wins a knight, but it leaves the queen far from the king and the rook on the e-file open. The evaluation jumps from +0.7 to +5.0, and the engine preferred 19...Qh3. This is the moment the attack becomes decisive.

moves.comment: 20.Rxe7+ gives up the exchange with check to open the king.
20...Nxe7 accepts the sacrifice, but the engine preferred 20...Kd8 and the evaluation becomes mate in four, which is a mistake.

moment.title: The exchange sacrifice on e7
moment.text: 20.Rxe7+ gives up a rook for a knight and opens the king to a queen check. Black's 20...Nxe7 looks natural, but the engine preferred 20...Kd8. The evaluation becomes mate in four after this recapture.

moves.comment: 21.Qxd7+ gives check with the queen and continues the attack. The evaluation shows mate in three.
21...Kxd7 accepts the queen, the only practical reply, and the mate is still three moves away.
22.Bf5+ checks the king with the bishop and drives it back. The evaluation shows mate in two.
22...Ke8 is the only king move that keeps the king on the back rank, and mate remains two moves away.
23.Bd7+ checks again, and the king has only one safe square left. The evaluation shows mate in one.
23...Kf8 is forced, leaving the king trapped on the back rank.
24.Bxe7# captures the knight with checkmate, ending the game on the e7 bishop.

moment.title: The final bishop mate
moment.text: 24.Bxe7# finishes the attack with a bishop check that the king cannot escape. The king is boxed in by its own pawns and the back rank. This is why the game is remembered as a model of sacrificial attack.

lessons: Keep your king's pawn shield intact before you launch your own queenside or central pawn advances.
When your opponent offers material, check whether the reply opens lines towards your king before you grab it.
Look for forcing checks and sacrifices in your own games, since a rook or queen sacrifice can end the game suddenly once the king is exposed.
